evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Both mod(mdg4)u1 and SuURES mutations partially suppressed the ct6 phenotype.

source: Interestingly, the double, SuURES and mod(mdg4)u1, mutant produced an additional suppression of the ct6 phenotype compared to that by mod(mdg4)u1 alone (Figure 5A, red arrowhead), which suggests that SUUR may contribute to the insulator function in the absence of Mod(Mdg4)-67.2.

claim: SUUR may contribute to the insulator function in the absence of Mod(Mdg4)-67.2.
source: Interestingly, the double, SuURES and mod(mdg4)u1, mutant produced an additional suppression of the ct6 phenotype compared to that by mod(mdg4)u1 alone (Figure 5A, red arrowhead), which suggests that SUUR may contribute to the insulator function in the absence of Mod(Mdg4)-67.2.

claim: Mod(Mdg4) was largely dispensable for underreplication in pericentric heterochromatin.

source: Notably, MERCI is not limited to analyses of known polypeptides since it is readily amenable to fractionation of native factors based on a correlation with their biochemical activities in vitro.

source: Although a SuUR mutation decreased the insulator activity, the suppression was universally weaker than that by mod(mdg4)u1.

source: The translocation model is consistent with observations of an asymmetric, selective occupancy of SUUR away from its initial sites of deposition via Su(Hw)-Mod(Mdg4) binding toward inside of intercalary heterochromatin regions but not outside (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C; Filion et al., 2010), which may be facilitated by physical interactions between SUUR and linker histone H1 enriched in intercalary heterochromatin (Andreyeva et al., 2017).
